[10] FAQ Frequently asked questions. Everything you need to know about creating, managing, and optimizing WooCommerce product feeds with CTX Feed Pro. Why aren't my WooCommerce products showing on Google Shopping? + Your WooCommerce products may not appear on Google Shopping because of missing product data, feed errors, incorrect attributes, or Merchant Center disapprovals. With CTX Feed Pro, you can create and manage Google Shopping feeds with accurate attribute mapping, variations, filters, and automatic updates. How do I get my WooCommerce products listed on Google Shopping? + To get your WooCommerce products listed on Google Shopping, generate a product feed, link it to Google Merchant Center, and submit it for review. How do I sync WooCommerce products with Google Merchant Center? + Create a product feed for Google Shopping from your WooCommerce store and connect it to Google Merchant Center. Why aren't my WooCommerce product changes showing in Google Merchant Center? + Your WooCommerce changes may not appear in Google Shopping if your feed hasn’t updated or synced with Google Merchant Center. Why is my WooCommerce price different from the price shown on Google Shopping? + An outdated feed, incorrect sales/ regular price mapping, or Merchant Center Updates can all be the causes of price differences. Why does Google Merchant Center disapprove of my WooCommerce products? + Google Merchant Center may disapprove products because of missing attributes, incorrect product data, feed errors, or policy violations. How do I fix missing GTIN, MPN, or Brand information in Google Merchant Center? + Use Dynamic Attribute (IFTTT rules) to conditionally fill missing GTIN/ MPN/ Brand from other product fields, or set a static default value where applicable. If genuinely unavailable, map the "identifier_exists = no" attribute so Google accepts the listing without those fields. Also check that Smart Filter isn't excluding products that already have this data. How do I map WooCommerce product categories to Google product categories? + In the feed's Category Mapping section, match each WooCommerce category to Google's official taxonomy from a dropdown/search list - this sets the required google_product_category field per category. You can also add product_type separately for your own category labels. Mapping is done once per feed and applies to all products in that category automatically. Can I generate a Google product feed with CTX Feed? + Yes. Both the free version and CTX Feed Pro allow you to generate a fully compliant Google product feed. They both include a ready-made Google Shopping template that automatically sets up all the required data attributes demanded by Google Merchant Center. Can I send a product feed directly to Google Merchant Center? + CTX Feed generates a feed URL, not a direct API push. You submit that URL in Google Merchant Center (Products → Feeds → Add via "Fetch file") and Google pulls it on your set schedule. There's no built-in one-click direct submission to Google's API. How do I keep my product feed updated automatically? + Set the feed's auto-update schedule in Feed Manager - CTX Feed Pro offers 5, 15, or 30-minute cron intervals (free version offers 1hr–1week). Once set, the feed regenerates automatically from live WooCommerce data with no manual re-export needed. How soon do product changes appear on advertising platforms? + Depends on two factors: your CTX Feed cron interval (as fast as 5 min on Pro) regenerating the feed file, plus how often the ad platform itself re-fetches your feed URL (Google/Meta typically pull every few hours, regardless of your update speed). So changes are reflected in your feed file quickly, but visible on the platform only after their next fetch cycle. How many products can CTX Feed support in a feed? + Unlimited. There is no cap on the number of products you can include per feed, and there is no limit on the number of separate feeds you can create. Can I choose which products are included in a feed? + Yes - use Smart Filter or Advanced Filter to include/exclude products by category, price, stock status, tags, or other attributes, or manually select specific products for a feed. Can I create multiple feeds for different channels, countries, or product groups? + Yes - you can create unlimited feeds, each independently configured for a specific channel, country/language, or product group (via filters/category selection), with its own template, mapping, and schedule. Does CTX Feed support WooCommerce variable products and variations? + Yes - you can choose to feed only the parent variable product, only specific variations (default, first, or last), or a combination of both, giving you flexible control over how variations appear in the feed. Which shopping channels and marketplaces does CTX Feed support? + CTX Feed supports 220+ channels via ready-made templates, including major ones like Google Shopping, Facebook/Instagram, TikTok, Pinterest, Microsoft Shopping (Bing), Etsy, Snapchat, and various regional marketplaces (idealo, PriceRunner, PriceSpy, etc.), plus custom XML/CSV templates for any channel not pre-listed. Is CTX Feed compatible with WPML and multilingual WooCommerce stores? + Yes - CTX Feed is fully compatible with WPML, Polylang, and TranslatePress, letting you generate feeds with translated product content per language. What should I do if my product feed isn't generating correctly? + Check CTX Feed > Status for PHP execution time/memory limits and WP-Cron status first. Then verify your filters aren't excluding all products, category/attribute mappings are complete, and try manually regenerating the feed to isolate whether it's a server timeout or a mapping/data issue. If it persists, check the per-feed log or contact support with your Status tab details. Stop fighting feeds. Start shipping orders. Once set up, add-ons appear on product pages just above the add to cart button. Ready to increase your store’s flexibility? Start using Product Add-Ons today. Frequently asked questions What can I do with Product Add-Ons for WooCommerce? Product Add-Ons for WooCommerce is a product customization extension that lets you offer paid or free options directly on your product pages. You can add options like gift wrapping, engraving, monograms, custom messages, premium upgrades, rush fees, tips, or donations, and shoppers configure them while they browse, before they reach checkout. Options can be added globally across products or set up per product from the edit product screen. How can customers personalize products in WooCommerce? Product Add-Ons give customers a set of fields to personalize a product as they shop. It supports multiple choice options (shown as dropdowns, images, or radio buttons), checkboxes, short text, long text, file uploads, a date picker, quantity fields, and section headings. This makes it a fit for stores selling custom t-shirts, engraved jewelry, personalized cards, mugs, or made-to-order goods where shoppers need to add their own text, choices, or artwork. What field types does Product Add-Ons support? Product Add-Ons includes several field types you can mix and match on a product page: multiple choice (dropdown, image, or radio), checkboxes, short text, long text, file upload, customer-defined price, quantity, date picker, and heading. Text fields can be restricted to letters, numbers, letters and numbers, or an email address, and long text fields can have a character limit. Headings help you group related add-ons into clear sections. Can I charge an extra fee for add-ons? Yes. With Product Add-Ons, you can attach a price to an add-on as a flat fee, a percentage of the product price, or a fee that is calculated based on the product quantity. You can also apply a discount by using a negative value in the price field. This gives you flexible ways to price upgrades, services, and personalization without creating separate products. Can Product Add-Ons help increase my average order value? Product Add-Ons is designed to help you present optional upgrades and paid extras at the moment a shopper is deciding to buy. By offering paid options such as gift wrapping, express handling, premium materials, or add-on services right above the add to cart button, you give customers straightforward ways to spend a little more on each order. Because add-ons can be priced as flat fees or percentages, you can match the pricing to each type of upgrade. Can I collect tips, donations, or let customers name their price? Yes. The customer-defined price field lets shoppers enter a value that is added to the product total, which works well for tips, gratuities, or donations. You can set a pre-filled default price and, if you prefer, limit the allowed price range. This gives you a simple way to accept flexible or pay-what-you-want amounts without building a separate product. Can I show product options as images instead of text? Yes. Product Add-Ons supports image-based selections, so customers can see a visual of each option rather than reading a text label. This is helpful when the choice is easier to understand visually, such as a color, finish, pattern, or style, and it lets shoppers see what they are getting before they buy. Can I apply the same add-ons to many products at once? Yes. You can create global add-ons that apply across your store, or add per-product add-ons from the individual product's edit screen. Global add-ons help you keep options consistent across similar products, while per-product add-ons let you tailor options to a specific item. You can also import and export add-ons to reuse them between products or global groups. Does Product Add-Ons work with WooCommerce Subscriptions and WooCommerce Bookings? Yes. Both extensions are separate purchases. Does Product Add-Ons support conditional logic to show or hide options? Product Add-Ons on its own does not show or hide fields based on a customer's earlier selections. If you need conditional logic, where certain options appear only after a specific choice is made, the recommended route is to use Gravity Forms together with the Gravity Forms Product Add-Ons extension. That combination is designed for more complex, interactive product forms. What is the difference between Product Add-Ons and product variations? Product variations are best when you sell a fixed set of predefined combinations, such as a shirt in set sizes and colors, each of which can have its own SKU and stock. Product Add-Ons is better when you want to collect custom input or offer optional extras on top of a product, such as engraving text, a gift note, an uploaded image, or a paid upgrade. Many stores use both variations for the core product choices and add-ons for personalization and optional services. When should I use Product Bundles or Composite Products instead? Choose Product Add-Ons when you want to layer options, personalization, or paid extras onto a single product. If your goal is to sell several products together as one package, Product Bundles is designed for grouping related products into a bundle. If shoppers need to build their own kit from a set of components with their own choices at each step, Composite Products is built for that guided, build-your-own experience. Product Add-Ons focuses on customizing one product rather than assembling multiple products. How is Product Add-Ons different from Product Options and Fields? Both are product personalization extensions on the WooCommerce Marketplace, so the right choice depends on how much configuration you need. Product Add-Ons, built by Woo, covers the core add-on field types, global and per-product options, and flat, percentage, and quantity-based pricing. Product Options and Fields , built by Addify, offers a larger field set and rule-based options such as user-role targeting and dependent fields. If you want a broader field library and conditional-style rules out of the box, it is worth comparing the two. Who is Product Add-Ons best for? Product Add-Ons is a good fit for stores that sell personalized or made-to-order products, or that want to offer optional paid extras and services. That includes shops selling custom apparel, engraved or monogrammed gifts, printed items, cards, and stores that want to add gift wrapping, rush handling, tips, or donations. It is a practical choice when you need straightforward add-on fields and pricing without building a complex conditional form. When is Product Add-Ons not the right fit? Product Add-Ons may not be the best choice if you need advanced conditional logic where fields change based on earlier answers, since that calls for Gravity Forms Product Add-Ons . It is also not intended for bundling multiple separate products together or for building configurable, multi-step kits, which are better served by dedicated bundling and composite-product extensions. If you mainly need predefined, stock-managed combinations, standard product variations may be enough. Where do add-ons appear on the product page? Once you set them up, add-ons appear on the product page just above the add to cart button, so customers see and configure their options before adding the item to the cart. You can use heading fields to group related add-ons into clear sections, which keeps longer option lists organized. Can I make an add-on required before a customer buys? Yes. Many add-on types include an option to require input or a selection before the product can be added to the cart. This is useful when you need a customer to make a choice or provide details, such as an engraving name or a required service option, before they check out. Does Product Add-Ons work with the cart and checkout blocks? Yes. Product Add-Ons is listed as compatible with WooCommerce cart and checkout blocks and with High Performance Order Storage, so it fits stores using the current block-based cart and checkout and the newer order storage setup. It also works with Smart Coupons , including the gift card feature. Once set up, add-ons appear on product pages just above the add to cart button. Ready to increase your store’s flexibility? Start using Product Add-Ons today. Frequently asked questions What can I do with Product Add-Ons for WooCommerce? Product Add-Ons for WooCommerce is a product customization extension that lets you offer paid or free options directly on your product pages. You can add options like gift wrapping, engraving, monograms, custom messages, premium upgrades, rush fees, tips, or donations, and shoppers configure them while they browse, before they reach checkout. Options can be added globally across products or set up per product from the edit product screen. How can customers personalize products in WooCommerce? Product Add-Ons give customers a set of fields to personalize a product as they shop. It supports multiple choice options (shown as dropdowns, images, or radio buttons), checkboxes, short text, long text, file uploads, a date picker, quantity fields, and section headings. This makes it a fit for stores selling custom t-shirts, engraved jewelry, personalized cards, mugs, or made-to-order goods where shoppers need to add their own text, choices, or artwork. What field types does Product Add-Ons support? Product Add-Ons includes several field types you can mix and match on a product page: multiple choice (dropdown, image, or radio), checkboxes, short text, long text, file upload, customer-defined price, quantity, date picker, and heading. Text fields can be restricted to letters, numbers, letters and numbers, or an email address, and long text fields can have a character limit. Headings help you group related add-ons into clear sections. Can I charge an extra fee for add-ons? Yes. With Product Add-Ons, you can attach a price to an add-on as a flat fee, a percentage of the product price, or a fee that is calculated based on the product quantity. You can also apply a discount by using a negative value in the price field. This gives you flexible ways to price upgrades, services, and personalization without creating separate products. Can Product Add-Ons help increase my average order value? Product Add-Ons is designed to help you present optional upgrades and paid extras at the moment a shopper is deciding to buy. By offering paid options such as gift wrapping, express handling, premium materials, or add-on services right above the add to cart button, you give customers straightforward ways to spend a little more on each order. Because add-ons can be priced as flat fees or percentages, you can match the pricing to each type of upgrade. Can I collect tips, donations, or let customers name their price? Yes. The customer-defined price field lets shoppers enter a value that is added to the product total, which works well for tips, gratuities, or donations. You can set a pre-filled default price and, if you prefer, limit the allowed price range. This gives you a simple way to accept flexible or pay-what-you-want amounts without building a separate product. Can I show product options as images instead of text? Yes. Product Add-Ons supports image-based selections, so customers can see a visual of each option rather than reading a text label. This is helpful when the choice is easier to understand visually, such as a color, finish, pattern, or style, and it lets shoppers see what they are getting before they buy. Can I apply the same add-ons to many products at once? Yes. You can create global add-ons that apply across your store, or add per-product add-ons from the individual product's edit screen. Global add-ons help you keep options consistent across similar products, while per-product add-ons let you tailor options to a specific item. You can also import and export add-ons to reuse them between products or global groups. Does Product Add-Ons work with WooCommerce Subscriptions and WooCommerce Bookings? Yes. Product Add-Ons works with WooCommerce Subscriptions so you can add extra options and pricing to recurring subscription products, and with WooCommerce Bookings so you can offer upgrades on bookable products, such as an add-on treatment, a priority option, or a rush fee. Both extensions are separate purchases. Does Product Add-Ons support conditional logic to show or hide options? Product Add-Ons on its own does not show or hide fields based on a customer's earlier selections. If you need conditional logic, where certain options appear only after a specific choice is made, the recommended route is to use Gravity Forms together with the Gravity Forms Product Add-Ons extension. That combination is designed for more complex, interactive product forms. What is the difference between Product Add-Ons and product variations? Product variations are best when you sell a fixed set of predefined combinations, such as a shirt in set sizes and colors, each of which can have its own SKU and stock. Product Add-Ons is better when you want to collect custom input or offer optional extras on top of a product, such as engraving text, a gift note, an uploaded image, or a paid upgrade. Many stores use both variations for the core product choices and add-ons for personalization and optional services. When should I use Product Bundles or Composite Products instead? Choose Product Add-Ons when you want to layer options, personalization, or paid extras onto a single product. If your goal is to sell several products together as one package, Product Bundles is designed for grouping related products into a bundle. If shoppers need to build their own kit from a set of components with their own choices at each step, Composite Products is built for that guided, build-your-own experience. Product Add-Ons focuses on customizing one product rather than assembling multiple products. How is Product Add-Ons different from Product Options and Fields? Both are product personalization extensions on the WooCommerce Marketplace, so the right choice depends on how much configuration you need. Product Add-Ons, built by Woo, covers the core add-on field types, global and per-product options, and flat, percentage, and quantity-based pricing. Product Options and Fields , built by Addify, offers a larger field set and rule-based options such as user-role targeting and dependent fields. If you want a broader field library and conditional-style rules out of the box, it is worth comparing the two. Who is Product Add-Ons best for? Product Add-Ons is a good fit for stores that sell personalized or made-to-order products, or that want to offer optional paid extras and services. That includes shops selling custom apparel, engraved or monogrammed gifts, printed items, cards, and stores that want to add gift wrapping, rush handling, tips, or donations. It is a practical choice when you need straightforward add-on fields and pricing without building a complex conditional form. When is Product Add-Ons not the right fit? Product Add-Ons may not be the best choice if you need advanced conditional logic where fields change based on earlier answers, since that calls for Gravity Forms Product Add-Ons . It is also not intended for bundling multiple separate products together or for building configurable, multi-step kits, which are better served by dedicated bundling and composite-product extensions. If you mainly need predefined, stock-managed combinations, standard product variations may be enough. Where do add-ons appear on the product page? Once you set them up, add-ons appear on the product page just above the add to cart button, so customers see and configure their options before adding the item to the cart. You can use heading fields to group related add-ons into clear sections, which keeps longer option lists organized. Can I make an add-on required before a customer buys? Yes. Many add-on types include an option to require input or a selection before the product can be added to the cart. This is useful when you need a customer to make a choice or provide details, such as an engraving name or a required service option, before they check out. Does Product Add-Ons work with the cart and checkout blocks? Yes. Product Add-Ons is listed as compatible with WooCommerce cart and checkout blocks and with High Performance Order Storage, so it fits stores using the current block-based cart and checkout and the newer order storage setup. It also works with Smart Coupons , including the gift card feature. The plugin offers on-demand sync and scheduled sync for Facebook and Instagram catalogs, supporting programs such as Dynamic Ads, Facebook Shops, and Instagram Shops. Pre-requisites Create the necessary business accounts with popular sales channels. The plugin offers one-way on-demand sync and scheduled sync for Facebook and Instagram. Facebook/Instagram catalog sync is an alternate method to sync the WooCommerce products directly (not using a product feed) with Facebook and Instagram catalogs to take part in programs like Dynamic ads, Facebook shops, Instagram shops, etc. With this method, you don’t have to copy and paste the feed URL. This method works by allowing you to perform on-demand sync, using which you can sync products whenever any update is made, or products are added to your store. The product changes will be reflected(may take some time) within Facebook/Instagram catalog. Syncing WooCommerce products with Facebook/Instagram To sync WooCommerce products with Facebook/Instagram: Once the plugin is installed and activated , navigate to WebToffee Product Feed > Facebook/ Instagram Catalog Sync > Manage Connection . Click the Connect Facebook button and allow permission for WebToffee product feed & Sync manager plugin. Connecting to Facebook Login to your Facebook account in which you have set up your Business account. Choose the business account . If you have multiple business accounts, it is necessary to choose the account you wish to sync products. Click on Continue . Choosing business account Review the changes and click on Save. Reviewing changes Click on Got it to reach the Manage Connection tab and proceed with the product sync. To manage the connection in the business account, go to Business integrations . Connected Now you have established connection with your business account. You can get started with syncing products with Facebook catalog. Manage connection tab Navigate to the Sync Products tab. First, select a FB catalog(if you have multiple catalogs associated with your business account). Provide the Product description type between long and short. Specify the Products per batch. It is the number of products that will be processed in a single iteration. Increase or decrease the value based on your server performance. If you are not sure about it, leave it to the default. Click on Next . Step 1: General Settings In the next step, filter products you wish to sync with Facebook catalog using different criteria which include: Exclude categories – Excludes specific WooCommerce categories from syncing with Facebook catalog. Only include specific categories – Includes specific categories in the sync. Exclude tags – Exclude products associated with selected tags. Exclude out of stock products – Enable the option to exclude out of stock products. Choose variation – Choose among All variations , Default variation and Lowest priced variation . Click on Next to proceed. Step 2: Filter products In the next step, map the store categories to that of Facebook categories. Furthermore, you can edit the already mapped categories for Facebook by going to the category edit page. Product level category mapping is also possible with the plugin. Category mapping Click on Schedule Sync to schedule the process. Alternatively, to sync immediately, click on Sync now. Schedule sync Once the sync is completed, click the Check FB Catalog button. This will redirect you to the catalog. Check FB catalog There, you can view the synced items in your catalog. Items in catalog Deleting synced products from the Facebook catalog Synced products can be deleted using the Commerce Manager . In the Commerce Manager , click on the Catalog drop-down and select Items . This will list all the synced products in the right pane. Select the products you want to delete and click the Delete icon at the top. Delete synced product – Facebook catalogue Logs Logs section records the product sync status. It provides reasons for failure to sync if any, besides each record. Logs Log records are used for debugging purposes. In case of any product sync failure, you can refer to the log file by clicking on View Status . Viewing log Scheduled Sync This section lists all the scheduled processes and their statuses. Scheduled Sync The WooCommerce Product Feed & Sync Manager plugin supports direct on-demand and scheduled sync of WooCommerce products with Facebook and Instagram catalogs. text: Forum Guidelines – WordPress.org Forums Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Forum Guidelines Search for: Search forums Forum Guidelines In this article Table of Contents User Expectations Contacting the Moderators Guidelines Do not advertise on the support forums Do not offer to pay for help Do not post about commercial products Do not create multiple accounts Be mindful when creating links to external resources We reserve the right to manage the forums to the best of our ability In closing Last Updated: 25 July 2024 Welcome to the WordPress.org support forums! 😃 The forums is a volunteer-powered resource, available to all users of WordPress to help improve the quality of WordPress Core, plugins and themes and to help solve problems with WordPress. User Expectations As a volunteer-powered forum, users are expected to be kind, helpful and respectful to all, assuming the best intentions of people and trying to help make things better. Please also be aware that these are community forums, this means that all users are required to follow the Community Code of Conduct . Be aware that there is no obligation for support to be provided, including by the developers of themes and plugins hosted on WordPress.org. Be mindful to follow any and all reasonable instructions given by a forum moderator at all times, they are long time contributors with experience to know when action needs to be taken, or warnings need to be issued. Contacting the Moderators If a post needs moderator attention, there is a ‘Report this topic’ link on every thread. That will add the post to a queue moderators watch and follow up with many times a day. If immediate action is needed, or the situation is not limited to a specific post, users should come to Slack and post in the #forums channel. (In many cases, the FAQ already might have an answer to your question. Please remember that the moderators are also volunteer contributors and may not always be online to respond immediately.) Guidelines Do not advertise on the support forums The forums are not a venue to promote your own (or others’) plugins, themes, websites or services. You are also not allowed to request payment to fix someone’s site, please use jobs.wordpress.net for this. Do not offer to pay for help Do not offer to pay for services or help on the forums, please use jobs.wordpress.net for this. Do not post about commercial products Commercial plugins and themes are not sold on WordPress.org, therefore please use their respective websites for support and reviews. For support of commercial themes or plugins, go to their official support channel. In order to be good stewards of the WordPress community, and encourage innovation and progress, we feel it’s important to direct people to those official locations. Doing this will provide the developer with the income they need to make WordPress awesome. Reviews of commercial plugins/themes are acceptable on WordPress.org when such reviews discuss functionality (including Software as a Services [Saas] solutions) or user-facing features. Reviews that are essentially payment disputes or are used to leverage support will be archived, with a reply that such disputes should be handled via private email. Do not create multiple accounts Individuals are limited to a single personal account. A company may register a brand account with a verifiable company email. We do not allow individual users to make multiple accounts, and consider this a bannable offense. Be mindful when creating links to external resources Public links in plugin or theme support topics may only be posted if they meet one or more of the following criteria: The link is to the plugin or theme authors own website. The link is to the plugin or theme authors own support website. The link is posted by the plugin or theme author themselves (or registered support users) to an external resource related to the topic. The link is to resources on the WordPress.org website. The link is to a reputable image-sharing service for screenshots. We reserve the right to manage the forums to the best of our ability We do our best to keep the forums friendly and safe for all users and developers. In order to do so, topic content may be moderated and users may have their access restricted, should the moderation team feel it is appropriate. We aim to use this power lightly and as sparingly as possible, however in severe cases, users may be suspended and posts removed entirely. Common reasons for edits or suspensions include but are not limited to: Violations of the WordPress Community Code of Conduct . Spamming . Unhelpful responses including but not limited to unvetted AI-generated responses or simple copy-and-paste of internet search results that aren’t specifically helpful to the thread starter. Posting personal information of other people (including but not limited to email, name, job, gender, living situation, location, etc). Posting private communication in the public forums or Slack. This includes direct messages, emails, support tickets, or other off-WordPress.org communication. Posting or accepting offers or requests for login information to a site. While plugin and theme authors may ask for this on their own support systems, they may not do so on WordPress.org for liability reasons. Harassment, threats, or abuse via any of WordPress.org’s systems or events (such as meetups or WordCamps). This includes actions such as following people to social media to continue a disagreement or complaint. Posting broad questions about opinions, such as “who is the best web host?” or other similar discussion topics that are not directly related to WordPress, its themes, or plugins. Posting only to solicit feedback for a site, theme, or plugin. Posting in ALL CAPS or abusing formatting (such as bolding the entire topic). Seeking legal advice or threatening legal action, including lawsuits. Please note that neither the list of examples above, or bannable offenses are exhaustive. Each and every post and interaction is judged on its own merits. In closing And that’s all. Enjoy your stay at the forums! Oh.. And, when you’re done, please mark your topic as “Resolved”. Thanks! Select the Settings icon at the top right corner of the video player, select Captions , and then specify your language. Having your products added automatically from your online store to Merchant Center is a faster and easier way to get them discovered across Google. If you make any changes to your online store, such as changing your product prices or removing a product, these changes are also automatically reflected on Google. This article explains how to automatically submit and manage your product data in Merchant Center. On this page How it works Enable automatic product submission Manage automatically added product data CSS guidance FAQs How it works Google automatically finds and adds your products to Merchant Center by: Discovering products : We scan your website to find product pages. Extracting information : We read the structured data on those pages to understand product details like title, price, and availability. Submitting to Merchant Center : We format that information and deliver it to your Merchant Center account, ready for use in Shopping ads and other marketing methods. Enable automatic product submission Google can automatically add any new products that are added to your online store to Merchant Center. To do this, you’ll need to: Use structured data to add detailed information about your products to your online store. Allow Google to collect this information. Verify and claim your online store’s website by linking it to your Merchant Center account . To avoid duplicate entries, products that are already included in other data sources won’t be added to Merchant Center. Learn more about managing your data . Create your automatic data source To create a data source in your Merchant Center: Go to the “Products” section. Under the “All products” tab, select Add Products . If you already have products in your Merchant Center, a drop down menu will appear. Select Add another product source . Select the Add products from [online store] card, with "[online store]" being your store's website URL. Note : If you don’t have the option to select the Add products from [online store] card when creating a data source in your Merchant Center account, ensure: Your structured data markup is correctly implemented for all required attributes. Learn more about how to Set up structured data for Merchant Center. Your account isn't suspended. Your site has the correct robots.txt settings, and Googlebot isn't blocked. Learn more about fixing issues with robots.txt . Steps to find the automatically added products In your Merchant Center , select the Settings in the left navigation menu. Select Data sources . Under the “Product sources” tab, the “Found by Google” section provides details of products that have been added automatically to your Merchant Center. Manage automatically added product data There are 2 options for displaying your products on Google: Automatically through organic search : Google uses structured data on your website to show basic product information in search results. This happens automatically, even if you don't have a Google Merchant Center account. Enhanced visibility through automated data sources : By opting into automated data sources in Merchant Center, you can gain more control over your product information and how it appears on Google Shopping and other surfaces. This includes richer product details, Shopping Ads, and more. Note : To avoid duplicate entries, if the same product is both automatically found on your online store and uploaded by you in a data source, we’ll keep the version you uploaded and remove the one that was automatically added. Automated data sources Opting in : Allows Google to automatically add and manage products from your website to your Merchant Center account, providing enhanced visibility and control over your product data across Google surfaces . Opting out : Stops Google from automatically adding products. However, basic product information might still appear in organic Google Search results based on your website's structured data, but with fewer management options. You'll find options to configure automated data source sections in a couple of areas of Merchant Center: "Data sources” tab : Allows you to edit countries, stop managing products, disable ads for products found by Google, and hide all automatically found products. “Products” tab : Allows active AFE merchants to enable ads, non-active merchants to activate AFE when enrolled, and for the exclusion of individual products. Controlling "Found by Google" products There are a variety of controls in the “Found by Google” data source. Hide all automatically found products You can use attribute rules to hide specific groups of automatically found products that you don't want to show on Google (for example, products from a certain brand or below a specific price). Use an attribute rule to set the Pause [pause] attribute to all for the products you want to hide. After 14 days, these products will be automatically archived. To prevent unwanted products from being crawled in the first place, it's recommended to use the data-nosnippet [data-nosnippet] HTML attribute on your website. Note : You can also archive automatically found products directly from the product list in Merchant Center. If you opt out of automated data sources in Merchant Center, Google will no longer automatically add products to your product data source. This may reduce traffic to your online store, but links to your products will still appear on Google Search and other surfaces where crawled data appears today. If you no longer want the products on your site to appear on Google Search and these other surfaces, you can add a 'noindex' tag to the product pages. Learn more about showing products on Google . Note : It can take up to 4-8 hours to fully hide "Found by Google" products in Merchant Center. Stop managing products If your Merchant Center account is using Shopping Ads , you can include or exclude automatically added products in Shopping Ads. To do this: Select the 3 dot menu icon in the “Action” column. Select Stop managing products . You can also remove all automatically added products by deleting the relevant data source. Note that Google may still show basic product information from organic search results even when a merchant selects "Stop managing products". If you don’t want the products on your site to appear on any Google Search, you can add a " noindex " tag to the product page. To add products back into your Merchant Center account, select the Start managing these products button that’s available when the Found by Google data source is inactive. Manage how products “Found by Google” are used in Ads If you enable ads for “Found by Google” products, your Google Ads campaigns may include additional products found now or in the future and in additional locations. Review your Google Ads campaigns’ product and location settings to check that products still show in their intended locations. If you wish to remove the products that are found by Google: Select Data sources under the Settings menu on the left hand panel in your Merchant Center account . Under “Products”, select the 3 dot menu icon in the “Action” column. Select Hide all automatically found products . After the exclusion setting is selected, any additional products found on your online store won't be used in your ad campaigns. Troubleshoot disapproved products We’re always working to improve the accuracy of the crawled information and increase the proportion of fully approved and quality items that are added through automatic website crawling. Having your products added automatically to Merchant Center is generally a faster and easier way to get them discovered across Google. However, you can always opt to hide the automatically added items, or stop managing them in Merchant Center altogether. Note : To help maintain a healthy product catalog, Google will now automatically archive products if we detect crawling issues (such as a broken landing page or an inaccessible image). This removes problematic products from your active list without requiring manual intervention. However, you can view or manually restore these products at any time from your archive folder, or Google will automatically restore them once the underlying issues are resolved. CSS Guidance If you're a Comparison Shopping Service, refer to How to start showing products on behalf of your merchants . Frequently asked questions How do I opt-in and opt out of products added automatically from my online store to Merchant Center? There are a variety of methods you can use to control where your products surface across Google. Control your product visibility through: Merchant Center : Navigate to the "Data Sources" or "Products" tabs to adjust settings related to automatic product submission and Shopping Ads participation. CSS Dashboard : Contact your Comparison Shopping Service provider to modify default settings for automatic product submission. How does eligibility work? Eligibility for automatic product submission depends on Google's ability to crawl and extract product data from your website effectively. Will any of my products get disapproved? Google employs automated systems to identify and remove products that potentially violate our policies , but this may not be 100% accurate. To ensure your products remain compliant and your account active, regularly review your product data in Merchant Center to check if any issues need to be fixed . How do I exclude certain products added by Google? In your Merchant Center account, select the Products tab in the left hand panel. Hover over the product you would like to exclude. From here, a box that says “This product is showing on Google” will appear. Uncheck “Show on Google”. If you want to control product visibility in your Google Ads campaigns you can use the listing groups feature in Performance Max campaigns , and Product Groups in Shopping campaigns . Will I be able to add products to multiple data sources? To avoid duplicate entries, products that are already included in other data sources won’t be added to Merchant Center. How frequently is my product data being crawled and processed by Google? Google checks your website at least once every 24 hours for new products and reflects the new products or updates on Merchant Center. Was this helpful? How can we improve it? Submit Need more help? text: Caused multiple site crashes - [Meta for WooCommerce] Review | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Plugin: Meta for WooCommerce / Caused multiple site crashes Search for: Search forums Caused multiple site crashes Jonas (@gnuworld) 1 month, 4 weeks ago Not built with the performance or stability of larger WooCommerce stores in mind whatsoever. We ran this on a dedicated VPS with 8 CPU cores and 24 GB RAM, and its catalogue/feed syncing brought the site to its knees on more than one occasion. The plugin handles catalogue syncing, feed generation, Meta tracking and related background processes, but provides no useful control over batching, throttling or scheduling resource-intensive sync jobs. In our case, catalogue/feed activity coincided with extremely aggressive meta-externalads crawling of the store, including hundreds of requests per minute. Combined with the plugin’s own sync/background workload, this generated enough load to destabilise Redis/object caching and make both the storefront and WordPress admin extremely slow or unavailable. Disabling the plugin immediately restored normal performance. There are also numerous reports from other users involving failed feed-generation jobs, repeated scheduled-action retries, excessive CPU usage and heavy catalogue syncing. For a small catalogue it may be fine, but I would be very cautious about running it on a larger WooCommerce store. We ultimately replaced it with separate dedicated plugins for Meta Pixel/CAPI tracking and catalogue feed generation, giving us much better control over each process. Viewing 1 replies (of 1 total) Plugin Support iodic (@iodic) 1 month, 4 weeks ago Hi @gnuworld , Sorry for the disruption this caused. The plugin does not currently offer settings to batch or throttle product feed generation. The meta-externalads requests come from Meta’s web crawler rather than the plugin’s background queue. That traffic can be controlled separately through robots.txt or rate limiting at the server or CDN layer — but note that it can affect ad performance if it’s rate-limited aggressively. If you’re open to it, please open a support thread with your system report and the details and logs from one of the failed wc_facebook_regenerate_feed actions under WooCommerce → Status → Scheduled Actions. It only recently clicked that the common denominator between the two sites was this plugin. On deactivating it, the two sites loaded around 3-4 times quicker, both front end and back end, and the lengthy waits have disappeared. Couple this with the ‘lifetime updates and support package’ which we paid for, and now no longer get support from, and the is no way we could recommend this plugin. title: Great for Merchant Center feeds, but conversion tracking creates conflicts with - [Google for WooCommerce] Review | WordPress.org
text: Great for Merchant Center feeds, but conversion tracking creates conflicts with - [Google for WooCommerce] Review | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Plugin: Google for WooCommerce / Great for Merchant Center feeds, but conversion tracking creates conflicts with Search for: Search forums Great for Merchant Center feeds, but conversion tracking creates conflicts with virdislucas (@virdislucas) 3 months, 1 week ago I’ve spent several weeks testing this plugin on a live WooCommerce store together with Google Ads, Google Analytics 4 and Google Tag Manager. The plugin does an excellent job syncing products with Google Merchant Center and generating the product feed. Unfortunately, the tracking side of the plugin causes several problems. Here are the main issues I encountered: The plugin automatically creates Google Ads conversion actions after connecting an existing Google Ads account, even when I explicitly selected that I already have campaigns and an existing tracking setup. During the campaign creation process, it immediately tries to create Google Ads campaigns instead of simply allowing Merchant Center synchronization and statistics. Purchase tracking appears to be sent automatically by the plugin, even when I use Google Tag Manager (GTM4WP) as my only tracking solution. There is no clear option to completely disable all conversion tracking while keeping only the product feed functionality. Even with Enhanced Conversions disabled inside the plugin, purchase-related data still appears to be transmitted, making it difficult to understand which source is sending conversions. The automatically generated conversion actions create conflicts with existing GTM implementations and can result in duplicate purchase events or very difficult debugging. The plugin mixes Merchant Center, Google Ads tracking and campaign management into one package. Many advanced users only need Merchant Center synchronization and product feeds. My current setup is: WooCommerce Google Tag Manager (GTM4WP) Google Analytics 4 Google Ads conversion tracking through GTM Google Merchant Center In this setup I want GTM to be the only source of conversion tracking, while the plugin should only manage the product feed. Suggestions: Add a “Feed Only” mode. Allow disabling all Google Ads conversion tracking. Do not automatically create Google Ads conversion actions. Do not automatically create campaigns unless the user explicitly requests it. Separate Merchant Center functionality from Google Ads tracking. Provide clearer documentation about which events are sent automatically and how to disable them. The feed functionality is very good, but the automatic tracking behavior makes the plugin difficult to use together with professional GTM implementations. Viewing 4 replies - 1 through 4 (of 4 total) Plugin Support Saravanan S, a11n (@simplysaru) 3 months, 1 week ago Hi there, Thanks for taking the time to share your experience — and glad to hear the Merchant Center feed sync is working well for you! Regarding the conversion tracking conflict with GTM4WP: this happens because both plugins are trying to handle the same tracking events (like purchase conversions and e-commerce data layer pushes) on the same pages. When two plugins inject overlapping tracking scripts, they can interfere with each other — duplicate events, blocked scripts, or one overriding the other. Google for WooCommerce is designed as a single, integrated solution for Google services — syncing your product feed to Google Merchant Center, running Google Ads campaigns, and measuring their performance with its built-in Google tag and conversion tracking — all managed directly from your WooCommerce dashboard . As a result, it includes its own measurement layer rather than relying on a separate Tag Manager setup. The plugin is built for a typical WooCommerce user looking to improve sales in their store using marketing options from Google services. Advanced users can always find ways to turn off certain functionality via custom code. That said, the long-term vision for Google for WooCommerce is to be the single plugin for all Google integrations on the WooCommerce platform — so it wouldn’t be surprising to see its capabilities expand further over time. Hope that helps clarify things! Thread Starter virdislucas (@virdislucas) 3 months, 1 week ago Thank you for your explanation. I completely understand the philosophy behind having a single plugin for Google services, and I agree that it is suitable for many WooCommerce users. However, I believe there is still an important usability issue for stores that already have a complete Google Tag Manager implementation. In my case, both “Improve conversion accuracy (Enhanced Conversions)” and “Send Enhanced Conversions data to Google Ads” are disabled. Despite this, the plugin still creates Google Ads conversion actions and continues to inject Google Ads measurement/tracking code and purchase-related events automatically. This makes it very difficult to understand which component is responsible for sending conversion data: Google Tag Manager Google for WooCommerce or both For users who already use GTM as the single source of truth for Google Ads and GA4 tracking, this creates unnecessary complexity and can lead to conflicts during debugging. My suggestion is to add a dedicated “Feed Only” mode that: Syncs products with Google Merchant Center. Does not create Google Ads conversion actions. Does not inject any Google Ads or Google Tag measurement code. Does not send purchase or remarketing events. Leaves all tracking entirely to Google Tag Manager. This would make the plugin much more flexible for agencies and advanced users, while keeping the current all-in-one experience for users who prefer automatic setup. During troubleshooting with Google Tag Assistant and GTM Preview, it is not always obvious which events originate from Google Tag Manager and which originate from Google for WooCommerce. A clear option to completely disable the plugin’s measurement layer would make debugging significantly easier. This reply was modified 3 months, 1 week ago by virdislucas . Plugin Support Saravanan S, a11n (@simplysaru) 3 months, 1 week ago Hey there, Thanks for the detailed follow-up — your points about the debugging difficulty when multiple tracking sources are active are well taken. To clarify how the plugin’s tracking layer works: the Enhanced Conversions toggles control whether hashed first-party customer data (name, email, address) is sent alongside conversion events to improve attribution accuracy. Disabling those settings stops that additional data from being sent, but it doesn’t disable the underlying Google tag or the conversion events themselves. Those are part of the plugin’s core measurement layer, which powers the campaign analytics dashboard inside WooCommerce and feeds performance data back to Google Ads for campaign optimization. Google for WooCommerce is built to handle the full integration loop — product feed, campaign management, and conversion measurement — as a single connected system. The tracking isn’t a separate, optional add-on; it’s what connects your product feed to campaign performance reporting. That’s the reason the plugin manages its own Google tag rather than deferring to an external Tag Manager setup. For stores that already manage all Google tracking through GTM, the recommended approach is to keep using your current GTM implementation for tracking and use custom code to disable any tracking that Google for WooCommerce adds. There are documented workarounds using custom code in the forums. I’ll note your “Feed Only” mode suggestion as a feature request, though we can’t make any promises on timing given the current roadmap priorities . We appreciate the detailed feedback — it helps the team understand how agencies and advanced users work with the plugin. Plugin Support Jason Kytros (@jasonkytros) 2 months, 1 week ago Hey @virdislucas , Thank you for your detailed feedback. The plugin has the woocommerce_gla_disable_gtag_tracking filter that can be used to disable Google Ads tracking. Here’s a snippet for that: add_filter( 'woocommerce_gla_disable_gtag_tracking', '__return_true' ); If you are not sure how to install snippets like this, I propose that you use a plugin such as Code Snippets . Can you please give this a try and let me know if the double tracking issue is resolved? Viewing 4 replies - 1 through 4 (of 4 total) You must be logged in to reply to this review. text: Requires Woocommerce have full control of your ads account - [Google for WooCommerce] Review | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Plugin: Google for WooCommerce / Requires Woocommerce have full control of your ads account Search for: Search forums Requires Woocommerce have full control of your ads account Mehlman Medical (@theforwardmale) 1 week ago In order to connect, asks you to check boxes to agree to: 1) Manage Google Ads accounts and data; 2) Manage Google Shopping product listings; 3) Manage Google site verifications Doesn’t allow you to check only some. Requires all to proceed. Then after you do, a Google warning appears that says this allows Woocommerce to take full ownership of your ads account, including deleting ads, campaigns, tracking, etc. No way in a million years would I allow those permissions by a third-party app. That’s insanity. I think this type of thing is for smaller players with tiny businesses who don’t really see the bigger picture of this permission. Just allow for simple store connection to YouTube without any connection to the ads account whatsoever. This topic was modified 1 week ago by Mehlman Medical . This topic was modified 1 week ago by Mehlman Medical . Viewing 3 replies - 1 through 3 (of 3 total) Plugin Support Saravanan S, a11n (@simplysaru) 1 week ago Hi @theforwardmale , Thanks for raising this — I understand the concern, and it’s a fair thing to pause on before granting broad access to any app. To clarify what you’re seeing: the Google for WooCommerce extension connects to Google Merchant Center and Google Ads using Google’s own OAuth flow, and it requires you to grant all of the requested permission scopes. This is by design — per the documentation, “Failure to grant all requested authentication scopes will prevent you from using the extension.” There’s no supported way to connect while granting only a subset, because the extension needs those scopes to create/manage your Merchant Center feed, create/manage Ads campaigns, and verify your site on your behalf. You can read the setup details here: https://woocommerce.com/document/google-for-woocommerce/get-started/setup-and-configuration/ The “full access” warning you saw is Google’s standard OAuth consent wording for the Ads management scope — it’s shown for any third-party tool that manages a Google Ads account, not something specific to WooCommerce. A few things that may help if you’d rather not grant that level of access: You are in control at all times and can revoke access whenever you want. From the extension’s Settings tab you can click “Disconnect all accounts” to revoke the permissions, or remove access directly from your Google Account’s permissions page. (Note: revoking affects any site using that Google account.) See the “How do I remove/revoke WooCommerce access to my Google account?” section here: https://woocommerce.com/document/google-for-woocommerce/faq/ If you prefer not to grant the integration those permissions, you can set up and manage everything directly in your own Google Merchant Center and Google Ads accounts, and sync products using a feed instead (for example via the Google Product Feed extension). That keeps account management entirely on Google’s side. If you’d like, let me know what you’re trying to achieve (free product listings, paid campaigns, or both) and I can point you to the approach that fits best. Incase you weren’t aware earlier, this extension is developed by the core WooCommerce team with guidance from the Google team and is the official extension. Some of us don’t want that connection whatsoever. It’s not good enough to have the ability to revoke access; we don’t want to give that access to begin with. Purpose of using a plugin is so that we don’t have to have it be complicated with Dev/tech-type knowledge of the inner workings. On your end, you say, “This is easy. These users complain and are dumb.” But it should be simpler somehow without all the manual work. This reply was modified 6 days, 6 hours ago by Mehlman Medical . We take feedback seriously, but no, we don’t undermine our users by thinking they are dumb. On the contrary, we think you are smart, especially since you were asking about the permissions the app requires. My previous explanation was meant to help curious users understand where these permissions and prompts come from. Understanding these aspects isn’t needed to use the extension. Hope you find a plugin that matches your needs. This reply was modified 5 days, 2 hours ago by Saravanan S, a11n . title: Silent failure during setup caused by blocked third-party cookies - [Meta for WooCommerce] Review | WordPress.org
text: Silent failure during setup caused by blocked third-party cookies - [Meta for WooCommerce] Review | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Plugin: Meta for WooCommerce / Silent failure during setup caused by blocked third-party cookies Search for: Search forums Silent failure during setup caused by blocked third-party cookies tredneb (@tredneb) 3 months ago After struggling with this setup for far too long, and after the usual experience of trying to get help from the Meta Help Center (which was, unsurprisingly, not very helpful), I finally found the actual issue. The connection process fails if your browser blocks third-party cookies. The setup appears to work, shows that WooCommerce is connected to Facebook, and then the popup just goes black or gets stuck. There are no useful error messages, no clear indication of what went wrong, and the plugin logs only show that the access token is missing afterwards. The solution was to temporarily allow third-party cookies in the browser, complete the Meta connection, and then disable them again. A simple warning in the setup screen would have saved hours of troubleshooting. Expecting users to diagnose a silent OAuth failure caused by browser privacy settings is not exactly a great user experience. You must be logged in to reply to this review. title: Your Google Ads account has been suspended - [Google for WooCommerce] Review | WordPress.org
text: Your Google Ads account has been suspended - [Google for WooCommerce] Review | WordPress.org Skip to content Showcase Plugins Themes Hosting News Resources Learn WordPress Documentation Education Forums Developers Blocks Patterns Photos Openverse ↗ ︎ WordPress.tv ↗ ︎ About About WordPress Make WordPress Events Five for the Future Enterprise Gutenberg ↗ ︎ Job Board ↗ ︎ Swag ↗ ︎ Get WordPress Search in WordPress.org Get WordPress Forums Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Welcome to Support Guidelines Get involved Log in Skip to content Forums / Plugin: Google for WooCommerce / Your Google Ads account has been suspended Search for: Search forums Your Google Ads account has been suspended kennethrg (@kennethrg) 2 years, 3 months ago This plugin seemed like a simple way to add the structured data and product feed to my Woocommerce store to enable Google to list my products in their shopping listings. However, it’s not been particularly simple. The setup is an odd modal experience that takes over the entire WordPress admin screen, such that I can’t access any other parts of WordPress during the setup of this plugin. That turned out to be an issue because of a conflict with my caching plugin. I can’t say exactly why, but I had to turn off my object cache in order to get this plugin’s setup screens to display properly. Nonetheless, the setup of a new store connecting to a new set of profiles in Google seemed to work fine. However, after setup things have not gone so well. First, the newly created Google Ads account was immediately suspended, before I actually did anything with it (past creating it) either directly or through the plugin. The automated message from Google: “Your Google Ads account ‏878-475-9615 has been suspended for violating our Circumventing Systems policy. Suspended accounts are prohibited from showing ads in all locations.” Now, I was able to appeal the suspension that Google quickly restored it, but within an hour it was automatically suspended a second time. Since the Google Ads account is optional, I disconnected it from the plugin and hopefully that will help. A second issue I noticed is that the plugin adds a gtag tracker to my site, with no configuration options and no obvious way to disable this feature. Once I disconnected the Google Ads account (above) the plugin also removed the tracking code, which is one way of doing things, but it seems like there ought to be more options. What if I don’t want Google tracking my site? What if I already have Google Analytics set up and already have all the tracking tags I need? What if I didn’t realize that the plugin added the tracking code and didn’t know to warn my visitors of it? Finally, to the thing I actually wanted out of the plugin: the product feed to a Google Merchant account: This appeared to be a set-it-and-done configuration, but according to my Merchant Account there are problems with the feed as it was set out of the box. Specifically, it said that there is “Missing shipping information” and “missing identifiers [gtin, mpn, brand].” Despite configuring shipping information in the plugin, that information didn’t make its way to Google. Additionally, brand and product identifiers were not set during setup and there was no prompt on the need to set anything else. Fortunately the plugin has a way to customize the feed, and since I’ve done this before I knew what to do. However, it’s not clear that it’s working yet; I may have to wait a few days for Google to review my account before I can be sure. The product feed is brokered through a WordPress.com account, for better or for worse. I’m not sure if there’s a benefit to this to those using the plugin, but it means I had to connect my store to WordPress.com and there’s no feed I can view by hand to verify the information being sent to Google. I can verify the information that Google receives, but relying on this third party link seems like it’s just adding another point of failure. I guess we’ll see. I haven’t decided whether to keep using this plugin or not. I’ve had good experience with another feed plugin that doesn’t require WordPress.com. While this other plugin required a little more technical know-how to get it working, at least it didn’t claim to be fully automatic when it wasn’t able to be. We’ll see how things turn out over the next few days. This topic was modified 2 years, 3 months ago by kennethrg . Viewing 4 replies - 1 through 4 (of 4 total) pfa3665b06b114b (@pfa3665b06b114b) 2 years, 2 months ago Hey Ken, experienced the exact same, it was at the recommendation of Google Search and subsequently Google Merchant Centre that I installed and setup the plugin, like yourself had to create a new google ads account and link it, the following day this was suspended without warning. Were you successful after disconnecting the ads account in getting it restored and did you go for another plugin and if so which one is that? Thanks Paul Thread Starter kennethrg (@kennethrg) 2 years, 2 months ago I gave up trying to get the ads account working and just canceled it, since I had no plans to buy ads anyway. The plugin seems to be working ok at the moment otherwise. I did see one quirk regarding shipping fees, though. A Google shopping listing was showing an incorrect shipping fee, and I couldn’t figure out how to fix it. Google says shipping fees are managed via the API, but the plugin doesn’t seem to have any settings that would explain how it’s passing shipping fees through. So I might switch yet. Another plugin I’ve had good experience with is WooCommerce Google Feed Manager by WP Marketing Robot. It was a little quirky to set up and took some trial and error to get the feed in the right format, but it’s been working well for a couple years for a different WooCommerce store I work with. pfa3665b06b114b (@pfa3665b06b114b) 2 years, 2 months ago Thank you for your quick response, I have just disconnected it now and will appeal again. I have not been able to get it to sync at all with the Merchant Centre so far and no indication why it hasn’t synced, more investigation to be done but will check out the other plugin as well. Thanks again! Plugin Support Saravanan S, a11n (@simplysaru) 2 years, 2 months ago Hey there @kennethrg and @pfa3665b06b114b , Sorry to hear about your experiences with the extension so far. Please be aware that the extension only connects your store to your Google account and helps sync the products to the account. You are bound by the terms of service on your Google Account, and the Google team is in the best position to help you with the account issues. You can learn more about how shipping works and is synced with Google here . Please note that, the extension tries to sync your shipping rates, as accurately as possible, but sometimes when advanced configurations for calculating shipping rates exist on your store, it’s better to configure them manually. If your account has been suspended, sync will not continue. So please ensure it’s approved. This reply was modified 2 years, 2 months ago by Saravanan S, a11n .
